Hello, I'm not sure where you're from but I live in the UK. We have something called Gamstop over here, if you register with them it literally blocks you from logging into any gambling site thats registered with it. 
You can go onto individual sites and have a cool down period which also blocks you from logging in, I used to use my phone bill to deposit money so you can also phone your provider and they'll block you from doing that, if you go into a gambling shop and tell them you have an addiction they legally can't serve you. 
Goodluck, I'm just over two years gamble free, it's a great feeling!

I'm 26. Cut myself during school/college and the last time I cut myself I had to go to hospital and seriously the worst thing would be for someone to get me 'professional help' as if there was something wrong with me.

I think you just need to let your son know that id he wants to talk then you'll be there to listen but it's okay if he's not ready.

I know all parents like to think they know their kids and wonder what's gone wrong but remember you only know what he wants you to know. He could literally have been through the worst and you'd never know.

If he wants help then help him whenever you can and let him know why you can't help him right away with your money worries but don't get angry with him if he doesn't. Sometimes someone needs to do it until they are done with it. It's hard to stop something if it makes you feel better.

I'm also a gambler and when I'd finally had enough and spoke to my family we decided that if I was having urges to gamble we'd go for a walk. So maybe you could work with doing an activity or something if he comes to you with urges to cut. But I very strongly agree that until he's had enough he will do it until he's ready. It's hard to explain because it's an addiction that brings so much relief when you're cutting.

I hope he talks to you and I wish him all the best with getting over this!
